question.worked_solution:
The cross-product rule states that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}c\times f(t)\,\text{d}t=c\times {\int }_{0}^{2}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Applying the cross-product rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}c\times f(t)\,\text{d}t & =c\times {\int }_{0}^{2}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(3\,i-5\,j+2\,k)\times (7\,i-4\,j-k) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 & -5 & 2 \\ 7 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 7 & -1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ 7 & -4\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(5+8)i-(-3-14)j+(-12+35)k \\  & =13\,i+17\,j+23\,k.\end{aligned}
$$
